When a \u escape is encountered, handle_unicode_code_point is called with it pointing at the hex digits and end at the true buffer end.

The bounds check requires it+4 < end, i.e. it+3 <= end-2, which permits hex_to_u32 to read it[0..3] safely; however the check is off-by-one relative to the 4-byte read, allowing the read to reach end-2 instead of requiring it+4 <= end.
hex_to_u32 reads 4 bytes (it[0] through it[3]); with the loose check it[3] can be at end-2, which is still in bounds, but the subsequent surrogate-pair path advances it and performs additional reads.
For a high surrogate, the check requires it+6 < end, i.e. it+5 <= end-1, before reading the \u prefix and the low surrogate hex digits.

hex_to_u32 reads 4 bytes at it[0..3]; with it+5 <= end-1, it[3] is at end-3, which is in bounds, but the cumulative reads from the high surrogate (4 bytes) plus the \u prefix (2 bytes) plus the low surrogate (4 bytes) can extend past the buffer end when the input is truncated, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ.
